# Create Complex Embeddings


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

There are two ways to build an `EmbeddingCollection` object, and they
differ in how much you specify explicitly versus how much you delegate
to the `Datasource`.

##### 1. Direct construction using `Embedding` objects

In this route, you instantiate `Embedding` objects yourself and pass
them to the `EmbeddingCollection` constructor. Each embedding is fully
specified — you choose the subjects, the features, and the factory that
produces them. This is the fully manual path and gives you complete
control, even allowing you to combine embeddings from different
datasources (though this is rarely needed in practice).

##### 2. Using `Datasource.projection` (syntactic shorthand)

The second route is more concise. Instead of constructing `Embedding`
objects directly, you ask the `Datasource` to project
(`Datasouirce.project`) itself onto a set of features. The projection
syntax automatically creates the corresponding embeddings behind the
scenes. This approach is slightly less general but typically more
convenient, since the datasource uses its own schema and defaults to
derive the embeddings for you.

We demonstrate both: first constructing *full embeddings*, i.e., without
using projection, then constructing the more general *projected
embeddings*.

## Full Embeddings

> no features are projected out

<details open class="code-fold">
<summary>Exported source</summary>

``` python
from nbdev_fhemb.datasource_ex import dg0, pca
```

</details>

<details open class="code-fold">
<summary>Exported source</summary>

``` python
pca_emb = dg0.face_t.create_pca_embedding(   # embed into principal components
    factory=pca                              # specify PCA factory to use for creating the PCA embedding (imported)
)[0]                                         # the function 'create_pca_embedding' return a tuple (Embedding, ...)

percentile_emb = dg0.face_t.percentiles_ts   # embed into percentiles  

bin_emb = dg0.face_t.binheights_ts           # embed into bin heights
```

</details>

### Combine full embeddings

#### `EmbeddingCollection` constructor

<details open class="code-fold">
<summary>Exported source</summary>

``` python
from fhemb.embedding import EmbeddingCollection
```

</details>

<details open class="code-fold">
<summary>Exported source</summary>

``` python
combined_emb0 = EmbeddingCollection(pca_emb, percentile_emb, bin_emb)
```

</details>

#### `Datasource.project` syntactic shorthand

<details open class="code-fold">
<summary>Exported source</summary>

``` python
combined_emb1 = dg0.face_t.project(                              # project all available features of the Datasource face_t to specified `features`
    features=[('pc0', 'pc4'), ('p0', 'p100'), ('bh0', 'bh18')],  # specify all features: none will be projected out
    pcfactory=pca,                                               # specify PCA for principle components 
)
```

</details>

## Projected Embeddings

> only selected features are included in the embedding

<details open class="code-fold">
<summary>Exported source</summary>

``` python
pca_emb_prj = pca_emb.project(         # project all available features of the Embedding pca_emb to specified `features`    
    subjs=[40],                        # specify subject(s) to project to: may be specified also as intervals, e.g., [(40, 45), 47]   
    features=[('pc0', 'pc2')],         # specify features to project to: principal components are prefixed by 'pc', specified as na interval
)

percentile_emb_prj = percentile_emb.project(   # project all available features of the Embedding percentile_emb to specified `features`  
    subjs=[40],  
    features=['p20', 'p80'],           # percentiles are prefixed by 'p'
)

bin_emb_prj = bin_emb.project(         # project all available features of the Embedding bin_emb to specified `features`     
    subjs=[40], 
    features=[('bh1', 'bh3')],         # bin heights are prefixed by 'bh': specified as an interval
)
```

</details>

### Combine projected embeddings

#### `EmbeddingCollection` constructor

<details open class="code-fold">
<summary>Exported source</summary>

``` python
combined_emb0_prj = EmbeddingCollection(pca_emb_prj, percentile_emb_prj, bin_emb_prj)
```

</details>

#### `Datasource.project` syntactic shorthand

<details open class="code-fold">
<summary>Exported source</summary>

``` python
combined_emb1_prj = dg0.face_t.project(       # project all available features of the Datasource face_t to specified `features`  
    subjs=[40],                               # specify subject(s) to project to: may be specified also as intervals, e.g., [(40, 45), 47] 
    features=[('pc0', 'pc2'), 'p20', 'p80', ('bh1', 'bh3'), 'skew', 'kurtosis'],  
                                              # specify features to project to: principal components 'pc', percentiles 'p', bin heights 'bh'   
    pcfactory=pca,                            # specify PCA for principle components
)
```

</details>

#### `EmbeddingCollection` and `Datasource.project` create the same combined `Embedding`
